title: 247. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Determining Range from a Graph
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Range of a Finite Graph Segment
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a graph given as a closed line segment.
questions.question: A graph is a line segment from \((-2,1)\) to \((3,5)\) with closed dots at both endpoints. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The range is the set of all \(y\)-values for which the graph has a point. The segment begins at \(y=1\) and ends at \(y=5\). Because both endpoints are closed dots, both values are included. Therefore the range is \([1,5]\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Use the lowest and highest \(y\)-values of the graph, and check whether the endpoints are included.

questions.concept: Range of a Ray with an Open Endpoint
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a ray whose endpoint is excluded.
questions.question: A graph is a ray that starts at \((-1,2)\) with an open dot and extends downward without bound. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The ray includes all \(y\)-values less than \(2\), but the open dot at \(y=2\) means \(y=2\) is not included. Therefore the range is \((-\infty,2)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Decide whether the starting point of the ray belongs to the graph.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range when a graph consists of two separate segments.
questions.question: A graph consists of two segments: one from \((-4,0)\) with a closed dot to \((-1,2)\) with an open dot, and another from \((1,3)\) with a closed dot to \((4,6)\) with a closed dot. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The first segment includes all \(y\)-values from \(0\) to \(2\), but \(y=2\) is excluded because the endpoint at \((-1,2)\) is open. The second segment includes all \(y\)-values from \(3\) to \(6\), with both endpoints included. Therefore the range is \([0,2)\cup[3,6]\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check each endpoint separately and decide whether its \(y\)-value is included.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a parabola from its vertex and direction of opening.
questions.question: A graph is the parabola \(y=x^2-4\). Its vertex is \((0,-4)\) and it opens upward. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The parabola opens upward, so the lowest point is the vertex at \(y=-4\). Since the vertex is on the graph, \(y=-4\) is included. The arms extend upward without bound. Therefore the range is \([-4,\infty)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Find the lowest point of the parabola and decide whether its \(y\)-value is attained.

questions.concept: Range of a Square Root Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a square root curve from its starting point.
questions.question: A graph is the curve \(y=\sqrt{x}+1\), starting at \((0,1)\) with a closed dot and extending to the right and upward. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The graph begins at \(y=1\), and because the starting point is a closed dot, \(y=1\) is included. As \(x\) increases, \(\sqrt{x}\) increases without bound, so the \(y\)-values extend to infinity. Therefore the range is \([1,\infty)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Find the lowest \(y\)-value of the graph and check whether that point is included.

questions.concept: Range of an Absolute Value Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of an absolute value graph from its vertex.
questions.question: A graph is \(y=|x|-2\). Its vertex is \((0,-2)\) and the graph opens upward. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The absolute value graph has its lowest point at the vertex \(y=-2\). Since the vertex is on the graph, \(y=-2\) is included. The arms extend upward without bound. Therefore the range is \([-2,\infty)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Find the lowest \(y\)-value of the graph and check whether it is attained.

questions.concept: Range of a Rational Graph with a Horizontal Asymptote
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a rational graph that has a horizontal asymptote.
questions.question: A graph is the curve \(y=\frac{1}{x-2}\). It has a horizontal asymptote at \(y=0\) and branches in the first and third quadrants relative to its asymptotes. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The graph approaches the horizontal line \(y=0\) but never reaches it, because \(\frac{1}{x-2}\) is never zero. All other real \(y\)-values are attained somewhere on the graph. Therefore the range is all real numbers except \(y=0\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Ask whether the graph ever reaches the \(y\)-value of the horizontal asymptote.

questions.concept: Range of a Graph with a Hole
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a graph that has a missing point.
questions.question: A graph is the line \(y=x+1\) with a hole at \((2,3)\). The line extends indefinitely in both directions. What is the range?
questions.explanation: The line \(y=x+1\) would normally attain every real \(y\)-value, but the hole removes the point \((2,3)\), so \(y=3\) is not attained. Every other real \(y\)-value still has a corresponding point on the line. Therefore the range is all real numbers except \(y=3\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether every \(y\)-value still has a point on the graph once the hole is removed.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of an upper semicircle from its endpoints.
questions.question: A graph is the upper semicircle \(y=\sqrt{9-x^2}\), with closed dots at \((-3,0)\) and \((3,0)\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The semicircle exists from \(y=0\) to \(y=3\). Because the endpoints at \((-3,0)\) and \((3,0)\) are closed dots, \(y=0\) is included, and the highest point at \(y=3\) is also on the graph. Therefore the range is \([0,3]\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: The range is the vertical span of the graph; check whether its lowest and highest \(y\)-values are attained.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a graph that consists of one isolated point.
questions.question: A graph consists of only the single point \((2,-3)\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The graph has a point only when \(y=-3\). There are no points for any other \(y\)-value. Therefore the range contains only the single value \(-3\), so the range is \(\{-3\}\), and option B is correct.
questions.hint: List every \(y\)-value for which the graph actually has a point.
